data.name: Vola
data.gender_notes: Vola is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The name Vola is derived from the Sanskrit word 'Vayu', which means wind or air. In Hindu mythology, Vayu is considered as the god of wind, and is one of the eight primary aspects of Lord Shiva. The name Vola is often given to girls born on a windy day or during a windy season. The name Vola carries the meaning “Wind” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit, Hindi. Parents who choose Vola usually hope their child will grow to embody wind and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: The name Vola represents the divine power of the wind, which is considered as a symbol of change, transformation, and purification in Hinduism. It is believed that the name Vola bestows the qualities of strength, courage, and adaptability upon the child.
data.etymology: Vola belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Wind.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Vola total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

data.cultural_impact: The name Vola holds significant cultural importance in India, especially among Hindu communities. Vayu, the deity associated with this name, is an integral part of Hindu mythology and holds a revered place in Hindu rituals and beliefs. Being named after Vayu is considered a source of blessings and good fortune, as it is believed that the child will grow up to be as strong, free, and unpredictable as the winds of nature.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Vola carries deep spiritual significance in Hinduism, as it is associated with Vayu, the god of wind. Vayu is considered to be the life force that sustains all living beings, and is believed to be present in every breath we take. By giving the name Vola to a child, parents are imparting a profound spiritual connection to the natural world and the divine spirit that pervades it. It is also believed that the child will be endowed with the qualities of Vayu - strength, courage, flexibility, and adaptability - and will be able to navigate the ever-changing currents of life with grace and poise.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Vola, meaning 'the one who carries the universe', symbolizes the divine power of holding the cosmos within oneself, embodying the infinite wisdom and strength of the universe.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Vola is mentioned in the Mahabharata as the name of a queen of the Vidarbha kingdom. The name Vola carried significant spiritual weight in that era.

modern_usage.modern_context: In today's interconnected world, the name Vola continues to be cherished by Hindu families globally. It is frequently featured on social media platforms where parents share their naming journeys, and Hindu name websites where expectant parents research meaningful names. The name bridges traditional Hindu values with modern Indian identity, making it relevant for contemporary families seeking names with deep spiritual and cultural significance.
